description: A personal Yu-Gi-Oh! experiment archive contains small card-database, deck, image/video, and GGUF inference tools; the tools have no shared entry point.
scope_audience: The README frames the audience as the author or hobbyists with local card databases, decklists, GPU/model assets, and related external tooling; those inputs are not bundled.

creativity.reason: The domain-specific combination of card statistics, deck experiments, visual selection/cropping, and a low-level GGUF wrapper is an interesting personal toolkit; global novelty is unknown.

current_usefulness.reason: Source includes real small utilities such as database-derived archetype statistics and tensor operations, but required databases, corpora, weights, and outputs are absent and the archive has no maintained workflow.

expected_usefulness.reason: If the stated hobby workflows are made reproducible for an owner with the required local data, they could save effort in card/deck analysis and media selection; no broader user benefit is established.

impl_progress.reason: Inspected scripts include card-stat aggregation and a substantial GGUF/ggml tensor wrapper, alongside notebooks and media helpers; no tests, data-backed result, or end-to-end workflow was run.

presentability.reason: README inventories individual tools, prerequisites, missing inputs, and status honestly, but there is no single install/run path or demonstrated output.

delivery_likelihood.reason: The archive is not maintained and depends on external private/local data and model assets; the individual scripts may remain usable with those inputs, but this was not exercised.

verification: Inspected README and generic implementation in stat.py and gg.py only. No card/deck/media payload, model, external module, tests, or execution was accessed.

evidence.locator: SQLite card-stat aggregation and YAML output
Tensor; view/shape operations; backend tensor access

contribution: A collection of independent hobby tools applies model inference, card statistics, deck experiments, and media selection to one domain; it is an archive rather than an integrated product.
alternatives_question: Which open tools support local card/deck analysis, representative replay-frame selection, and card-art cropping, and which of these tasks still require bespoke work for the author's intended workflow?
reason: The inspected source establishes meaningful personal implementation, but missing inputs, no unified workflow, and no comparative evidence keep current utility and differentiation provisional.
next_step: If public or repeat use is intended, isolate one representative task, provide a privacy-safe fixture and expected output, and document a reproducible entry point without sharing private datasets or weights.
